claim: By wheeling south-east inside Paris on 30–31 August, Kluck exposed the 1st Army's right flank to the Paris garrison and the new 6th Army; the Ourcq attack that opened the Marne struck exactly there.
historiography: Whether Kluck's turn was a blunder or the only way to keep touch with Bülow and pursue a 'beaten' enemy is still argued; Herwig treats it as a reasonable decision on the information available, made fatal by the thinned right wing and Joffre's redeployment.

evidence.note: chapters on Kluck's wheel and the Ourcq

claim: Instruction générale no 2 (25 August) created the mass of manoeuvre on the French left — the future 6th Army, railed from Lorraine — without which there was no flank attack to make on 5 September.
